name: Aphanostephus

project_scope.installer_dependency: A. riddellii is source-pool only; no canonical installation in this lane.
project_scope.range_note: Preserve A. skirrhobasis UNRESOLVED target-zone status.

look_here_first: Start with annual versus perennial habit; turn a head over to examine overlapping pale-margined phyllaries; use mature disc florets and magnified cypsela hairs for a confident species split.
shared_genus_traits: Small radiate Asteraceae heads with pale ray florets and yellow disc florets; color alone does not identify the genus.
Overlapping involucral phyllaries and a conical receptacle; mature fruit morphology is important for separating similar small daisies.

shared_structure_examples.plain: One daisy-like head contains many tiny ray and disc flowers.
shared_structure_examples.photo_role: same-scale front and side flower-head macro

shared_structure_examples.plain: Several overlapping rows of bracts wrap the underside of each head; inspect their pale margins.
shared_structure_examples.photo_role: underside of mature head with scale

shared_structure_examples.plain: The base of a mature central floret may be bulbously swollen in A. skirrhobasis.
shared_structure_examples.photo_role: dissected mature disc floret under magnification

shared_structure_examples.plain: Tiny hairs on the dry one-seeded fruit bend in different patterns between species.
shared_structure_examples.photo_role: matched microscope photographs of mature fruits

species_comparison_matrix.how_to_check: Examine roots and several mature plants; do not infer from a cropped flower photo.
Dissect fully mature disc florets under magnification; immature heads unreliable.

species_comparison_matrix.skirrhobasis: Curved or coiled predominantly in one direction
species_comparison_matrix.how_to_check: Matched magnified mature fruits; targeted regional-key verification pending.
Overlapping character; not a species separator.

look_here_first: Identify a composite head and check the underside phyllaries.
Record whole-plant life cycle and basal versus stem leaves.
Dissect mature disc florets and fruits when the species matters.
Leave uncertain plants at Aphanostephus until mature diagnostic material is available.
overlap_cautions: Both species have similar pale rays and yellow centers.
A. pilosus and small Erigeron may resemble these plants; compare receptacle, phyllaries, cypsela ribs and pappus rather than flower color.
The fruit-hair distinction needs an authoritative key and actual magnified specimen verification before any arrows.
